name: Google Merchant API Recovery Sprint
signal: Google Content API for Shopping sunset on 2026-08-18. Since 2026-09-01, clients without an active extension can intermittently receive HTTP 410 Gone; full decommissioning is planned for early 2027.
customer: E-commerce merchants, agencies and SaaS/PIM/feed vendors with custom Content API integrations that have not fully migrated to Merchant API v1.
pain: Intermittent failures can silently leave prices, stock and product listings stale, making the defect commercially damaging and harder to diagnose than a clean outage.
offer: Fixed-price recovery sprint: identify legacy Content API calls, map them to Merchant API v1, migrate product/inventory/account/reporting flows as needed, test and verify feed freshness.
distribution: GitHub code search for shoppingcontent.googleapis.com and content/v2.1 usage
E-commerce/PPC agencies with custom Merchant Center integrations
Merchants whose Merchant Center data source still reports Content API
evidence: Official Google documentation: Content API sunset 2026-08-18; progressive HTTP 410 failures from 2026-09-01 without extension; full decommissioning early 2027.
Merchant API is not a drop-in endpoint rename: architecture is modular and legacy customBatch behavior changes.
Public GitHub code still contains direct shoppingcontent.googleapis.com/content/v2.1 usage, although much of the searchable corpus consists of libraries/samples and is not itself a commercial lead.
Commercial migration/audit services already exist, validating willingness to pay but reducing differentiation.
gate: Do not create a public Rockrai experiment yet. First identify at least 10 commercially plausible organizations with evidence of a legacy custom integration or current 410/feed-freshness symptoms, and obtain at least one credible commercial-interest signal. If passed, proposed subdomain: merchant-rescue.rockrai.com.
risks: Major commerce platforms and feed vendors generally handle migration for customers, shrinking the addressable segment to custom integrations and lagging vendors.
Long advance notice means many competent teams have already migrated.
Public code evidence is noisy because official SDKs and samples dominate searches.
Google extensions can temporarily defer urgency for some projects.
decision: KEEP AS CANDIDATE; stronger than a future deadline because failures are already occurring, but lead-quality gate must be passed before building a landing page.
